method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21: (1) split the part into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye.

sections.meaning: Say 'wait for us' and hear; there are those who would not love any good to be sent down to you, but God singles out whom he wills for his mercy.
ideas: Hikers pausing on a trail so the stragglers catch up
A raised hand at a stream crossing
A man with folded arms glaring at a neighbor's laden fruit tree

sections.meaning: Whatever sign is cancelled or forgotten, God brings better or like it; whoever trades belief for disbelief has gone astray from the even way.
ideas: A hand replacing a dim old bulb with a brighter one in a dark room
A street lamp being swapped for a brighter lamp at dusk
A smooth level path and a walker lost in rough brush beside it

sections.meaning: Pardon and overlook; keep up prayer and alms, and whatever good you send ahead you will find with God.
ideas: A father smiling while picking up the pieces of a toddler's broken cup
A man answering a neighbor's shouting with a calm smile and a basket of fruit
A traveler arriving at a lit house to find the basket he sent ahead on the porch
Soil cross-section with a seed and its roots

sections.meaning: They say no one will enter the Garden but their own; 'bring your proof'. Whoever submits his face to God and does good has his reward. Each side says the other has nothing to stand on, though both recite the Book.
ideas: A face lifted to the sunrise with eyes closed
A person kneeling on a plain floor with open hands
Two men on the same cliff ledge each pointing at the other's foothold

sections.meaning: Whoever bars God's places of worship and strives for their ruin does great wrong; to God belong the east and the west, and wherever you turn, there is the face of God.
ideas: A plain hall with chained doors and boarded windows and weeds on the steps
An excavator facing a plain hall
A person turning in a circle on a plain with golden light on every horizon
A person lying on a dune under a sky full of light

sections.meaning: He is the Originator, and when he decides a matter he only says to it 'Be', and it is.
ideas: A hand presses a switch and a vast dark hall blazes with light at once
Sunrise breaks over a dark valley all at once
A seed becoming a tree

sections.meaning: Those who do not know ask why God does not speak to them or send a sign; the signs are clear; God's guidance is the guidance; those who read the Book as it should be read believe in it.
ideas: A man on a hill with arms crossed demanding a sign while birds fill the sunrise behind him
A compass resting steady on a flat rock at sunrise
A man absorbed in reading a book on a bench in dappled light

sections.meaning: Remember the favor, and guard against a day when no soul will pay for another.
ideas: A waiting hall of rows of chairs, each person alone with their own ticket
A line of hikers each carrying their own pack up a trail

candidates.principle: You who believe, do not say, "Attend to us," but say, "Wait for us," and hear. And for the disbelievers there is a painful punishment.
candidates.shows: Hikers stop on a mountain trail so that those behind can catch up.
candidates.prompt: On a mountain trail in clear morning light, a group of ordinary hikers in plain outdoor clothes have stopped and turned back, waiting patiently for a slower friend and an older hiker climbing up the trail to catch up. The hikers are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.

candidates.principle: You who believe, do not say, "Attend to us," but say, "Wait for us," and hear. And for the disbelievers there is a painful punishment.

candidates.prompt: At a stone crossing over a shallow stream, a man in plain clothes on one bank holds up one open hand to say wait, looking back toward a friend who is still crossing on the stepping stones, soft light. The man and the friend are in the upper two thirds of the picture. Everything that matters is in the upper part of the frame; the lower part is plain foreground.
